utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I understand that there are some issues you would raise first Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you very much. Yes, there are three brief issues and for the first one we would wish to go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second application is more of an embarrassment than anything else but it is going to made on behalf of both Defence team. You will remember, Your Honour, that last week that the Prosecution filed a motion to have a number of documents admitted in evidence, and Your Honour had requested the Defence to respond within three days of the Prosecution filing which in effect would fall today and require to us respond in the course of this day. Because of the events of last week, and the amount of preparation also involved in this witness and the next witness, it has proved extremely difficult for the Defence to be ready on time. We would therefore seek leave from the Trial Chamber for an extension of time perhaps until Thursday which would allow us to provide a meaningful response to the Defence to the Prosecution application. We also understand that the Prosecution would have no objection to the request being made. What we can indicate also to Your Honour which may, in a way compensate for this request, the two Defence will file a common response which may, at the end of the day, save some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, given that there will be a break of a week and a day, it would seem preferable if the outcome of this motion could be known before the break so that, as necessary, planning could occur during the break and the knowledge of what is the outcome. With that in mind, the Chamber would look to have your motion on -- your submissions on Wednesday rather than Thursday. Is that feasible?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is a third matter, Your Honour, very briefly which we would like to raise. You will recall that during the re-examination of the witness Mr. Tucker, Mr. Saxon raised a number of issues pertaining to one particular document which was the report prepared by the commission set up by Mr. Boskoski to look into the matters of Ljuboten. And in particular, Mr. Saxon asked the question of the witness as to the origin of the document, or, rather, how this document had come into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor. The Defence at the time had objected to the question being put and Mr. Saxon had indicated at the time that he stood corrected and withdrew his question. We had the opportunity to discuss this matter further with the Office of the Prosecution, and the Defence of Mr. Boskoski and the Prosecutor have agreed to a certain stipulation or specification which agreeable to both parties and I would wish to read it on the transcript. Having discussed the matter, the parties have agreed that it is not in dispute that the report prepared by the commission set up by Mr. Boskoski on 13 August of 2001, numbered 02-581/01, admitted as exhibit P378 was provided by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY no later than 18 September, 2001. That will be all, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it that is a matter that is accepted, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski, is there a matter you have to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no matter that I would like to raise, Your Honours. I left it to my colleague, Mr. Mettraux, on behalf of both teams to present these propositions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was there something about an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The expert witness -- the expert is in -- in The Hague in the gallery; therefore, he will follow the trial from the gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Is there any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In that case, we can continue. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If I could remind you the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You recall that that last week I asked you a number of questions about the representation of ethnic Albanians in public offices; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in response to a number of questions that I put to you, you said that what really counted were not the number of Albanians in elected positions but the number of Albanians working in ministries and so on. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Bushi, that at the time when you took up arms, the Macedonian state was attempting to increase the number of ethnic Albanians in public employment; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Bushi, that your activities, your criminal activities in fact made the process of integration of ethnic Albanian more difficult rather than facilitating as you claim you were attempting to do. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could wouldn't call them criminal activities and what you're saying, sir, is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 1D119, please. It is an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, the document that I will show to you, it will appear in Macedonian on your screen. This is a report from the Ministry of the Interior, it is the Department for International Cooperation and European Integration. It is dated 24th of April of 2001 and the subject is negotiation regarding training for newly recruited police officers in cooperation with the US embassy in the Republic of Macedonia. And if you look at the first paragraph in this document, I will read it out to. It says this: "It refers to a meeting of the 18th of April, 2001. The meeting was held in order to discuss assistance in the training of 500 newly recruited police officers with support from the US department of finance -- programme which is administered through the US embassy in Macedonia. If you look to the next paragraph it says this: "The training programme is aimed at increasing the number of police officers from ethnic minorities living in the Republic of Macedonia with priority given to ethnic Albanian candidates. The programme is to be completed by October 2002. Training will be performed successively in groups of approximately 100 candidates who will then be deployed to work in the area in which they reside, that is, areas which are predominantly populated by ethnic Albanian citizens." Mr. Bushi, were you aware of these measures being taken or undertaken by the Ministry of Interior to increase the number of ethnic Albanians within that ministry?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you should consider the fact that the war started on the 14th of February. This document is dated 18th April, while the first training started when the BDI became part of the coalition, ruling coalition.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But isn't the case, Mr. Bushi, that this programme sponsored by the United States had started to function in the year of 2000. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. And I don't know to what extent it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if you look down on the document it says this: "The following was agreed at the meeting. The immediate formation of a Ministry of Interior commission which will establish the criteria for admission as well as the exact number of candidates, 100, that need to be recruited in the first phase in addition to a publicity campaign in the channels of public information." And then it goes on to say: "The proportion of candidates that will be recruited, Director Kaziriski [phoen] recommended that 60 per cent be ethnic Albanians, 20 per cent Macedonian of the Islamic faith and members of other nationalities living in Macedonia, and 20 per cent ethnic Macedonians in order to maintain a certain level of balance which relates to the factual situation." Were you aware of these efforts being made between the Ministry of Interior, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These efforts began when the war ended. Before the war and when the war started, the Ministry of Interior made no efforts and the government at the time was not willing to carry out these changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, you will agree that on 24th of April 2001, what you call the war was still going on. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's the date of this report. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In fact your activities made this process, which was ongoing almost impossible. It is because of your actions that it could not go faster. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will also refer the Chamber to the evidence of Mr. Galevski on the 18th of July of 2007. It is at page 3725 to 3730.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'm also putting it to you that you were not content just to make the process more difficult but you actually made attempts or made sure that the process of integration of ethnic Albanians into ministries and other public offices would be difficult or -- impossible because if it did work out, it would deprive you of an excuse for your activities. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, sir. The integration should have happened in the 1990s up to 2001. While this integration in fact began when the Ohrid Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a village called Brest on the border between Macedonia and Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know what happened in the village of Brest during the first week of the month of March of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a conflict there; I don't know exactly. You mean in 2001, early 2001? Beginning of March? Well, yes, the war was ongoing at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall a particular incident on the 8th of March 2001, involving Mr. Boskoski and his then deputy minister, an ethnic Albanian by the name of Refet Elmazi. Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what Mr. Boskoski and Mr. Elmazi were doing in Brest at the time, they went there to try and open mixed police station, Albanian and Macedonian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. They went there on another mission. Refet Elmazi the deputy interior minister and Ljube Boskoski, the minister of the interior, they went there to appeal for the war to stop. They did not go there to open a police station of mixed composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that is not quite right, Mr. Bushi. I put it to you what they did is they went to Brest, both Mr. Boskoski and his deputy minister an ethnic Albanian, to try to open a mixed police station and what they did, they were greeted by members of your organisation who attacked them and murdered one of the police officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct that they went to open a police station of mixed composition. They went on another mission. They went to appeal to the citizens, to the villagers to stop the war. You know that the war started on the 14th of February, both Refet Elmazi and Ljube Boskoski were surrounded by former NLA soldiers at that time. And with the mediation of certain persons they were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the ethnic Albanian who saved Mr. Boskoski's life at the time was shortly after executed by a member of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which person are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Local ethnic Albanian who had provided shelter to Mr. Boskoski and a number of other members of the Ministry of Interior during the attack by your group.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true and I want to know which person you are referring to. Can you mention his name and last name? Maybe that will ring a bell, but as you're putting it now, I don't remember anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, concerning the incident in question we will refer the Chamber to Exhibit P45, that is the white book of the Ministry of Interior, in particular at page 110, that's N005-7606-0112. It is also mentioned in Exhibit P42, that Mr. Boskoski's book. In particular at N000-N607-ET-14. The incident was also discussed by a number of Prosecution witnesses, Mr. Galevski on the 18th of July of 2007, at page 3727 to 3728 and 3733; by Mr. Zoran Trajkovski on the 24th of September of 2007, at page 5561 to 5652; and also by Witness M-051 on the 27 of August of 2007 at page 4157 to 4158.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bushi, that your organisation also threatened ethnic Albanians and kidnapped a number of them with a view to prevent them from joining the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You would agree that if this had happened, it would be unlikely to contribute to ethnic Albanians joining the Ministry of Interior. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. At the time there were members of the ethnic Albanian community who were members of both the police and the army of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 1D18, please, 1-8. It is Exhibit 1D18, I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a report from the organisation OSCE. There is no Macedonian or Albanian version of this document, so I will read it out to you. It is a special report. It is called, human rights related complaints related to the ethnic Albanian armed group in the Tetovo area. And I will read to you the first two paragraphs of this document. It says this: "On Friday, July 20, the mission human rights specialist spent the day in the Tetovo area continuing to address human rights concern specifically related to the conduct of the ethnic Albanian armed group in that region. The allegations under investigation related not only to the group's treatment of ethnic Macedonian in the Tetovo but also towards persons in the ethnic Albanian community who objected to the ethnic Albanian armed group's activity or --" There are two words I can't read. Then goes on to say: "The mission specialist confirmed reports from the OSCE Tetovo area monitors that even during the cease-fire, the ethnic Macedonian civilian population north of Tetovo is under heavy pressure from the ethnic Albanian armed group to leave. This pressure takes the form of kidnappings, temporary detentions and serious persistent forms of intimidations and restrictions on the movements of civilians attempting to engage in order activities such as agriculture, shopping and going to work. The conduct of the ethnic Albanian armed group is consistent with an attempt to ethnically cleanse that area." Mr. Bushi, were you aware of those activity by your colleagues from the Tetovo area?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this is not true, that my colleagues from Tetovo carried out these activities. There is one truth, the -- this happened on the part of the Macedonian security forces when in Bitola they burned houses and they also kidnapped civilians from their own houses, Ruzhdi Veliu, Sulthan Mehmeti from Struga, Hani from Veleshta and other persons who were taken by the Macedonian police forces from their own houses. In Manastir of Bitola there was no NLA presence, but this is what the Macedonian security forces did in Manastir; they burned their shops, they burned the mosque. But what you are saying here is just a statement by one single person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting to you Mr. Bushi that every time your organisation is faced with accusations of crimes, you choose between three alternative explanations: One, it did not happen; two, the Macedonians did it; or, three, it was the splinter groups that did it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are facts, sir. This is not something that I'm making up. These are facts and that is why I appeal to you to show me a single case or an example of terrorism or criminal activity. You're just putting to me statements. You're not giving me any facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page of this document, please. And I will ask the registry to focus on the third paragraph on this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is still the same document from the OSCE and I would like to read a sentence which is in the middle of the paragraph started with the word: "The mission is most likely." And I will read it out to you. The OSCE said this: "As of 23rd July, the mission has received credible allegations that 25 persons have disappeared or are allegedly detained by the ethnic Albanian armed groups operating in the Tetovo area. This number includes ethnic Macedonian civilians and ethnic Albanians who were serving in the Ministry of Interior as regular officers or as reservists at the time of their disappearance." So what you and your organisation were doing, Mr. Bushi, in fact was to prevent or make it impossible or extremely dangerous for members of any ethnic group, Macedonian, Albanian or otherwise, to work in any of the ministries of the Macedonian government. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when this very -- when this very statement was put to a member of the OSCE, he was asked whether such kidnappings would create a disincentive for anyone to be joining the Ministry of Interior and he agreed. Would you also agree with that, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with this either.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the transcript of Mr. Bolton, 7 June 2007, page 1662 to 1664..

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you will remember that the Prosecution asked you a few questions about the Ohrid Framework Agreement and I also did so last week. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I also put it to you that the reason why the NLA was not involved in the negotiation or the signing of that agreement was whether the international community and the Macedonian authority regarded it as a -- let's say, an unapproachable partners for peaceful discussions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that the -- what the Albanian political parties came up with that was orchestrated by Ali Ahmeti and this goes for the Ohrid Framework Agreement as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting it to you, Mr. Bushi, that the international community, the people who negotiated or assisted the negotiation of the Ohrid Framework Agreement with the legitimate political parties in Macedonia wanted no business with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. There were negotiations at the time with our commander Ali Ahmeti. There were representatives from the international community. There were negotiations going on to put an end to the war and sign the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P45. That's the "White Book" and I will ask the registry to go to page N005-7606-0170; in the Macedonian, it will be N001-5211. This is at page 168 of the book in the English translation. I'll ask the registry to focus on the bottom of the page, starting with the words: "NATO condemns the violence." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to read to you is a statement made by the general secretary of NATO, Lord Robertson. It was made on the 24th of May of 2001. This is what he said: "I strongly condemn recent actions by extremist groups in the Republic of Macedonia, in particular their continued presence in several occupied villages and their attacks on government security forces. Their actions are imposing grave risk and hardship on the very people whose rights they claim to support. The regrettable casualties and damage caused by their conflict with government forces is the direct result of their unjustified occupation of towns and villages in the north of the country. "We must be very clear that the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia is an established and well-functioning democracy. It has recently formed a grand coalition involving the major ethnic Albanian political parties. This coalition is engaged in a broad-based effort to seek democratic solutions to the country's problems. I support these efforts and urge the government to continue to find ways of addressing the legitimate concerns of its public Slav, Albanian and others through democratic political means. There is no justification, none for any citizens of this nation, to take up arms against the government." And then he goes on to say this: "The future of the nation can only be decided by democratically elected individuals working through this peaceful political process. The international community will only work with these legitimate political representatives, not armed extremists. The men of violence, such as the leaders of the so-called NLA, have no place in this process. They have no democratic legitimacy and, thus, no place at the negotiating table. They cannot achieve with a bullet what can only be addressed through the ballot." You agree, sir, Mr. Robertson as Secretary-General of NATO, as well as all other political leaders, internationals and Macedonians, refused to deal with you when they negotiated the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. The negotiations about the Ohrid Agreement did not start on this date. They started later, and it is true that NATO was one of the guarantors of the signed Ohrid Agreement. To this day, negotiations are ongoing between Ali Ahmeti, as representative of our political party, and NATO representatives. To this date, I have not seen or witnessed any negotiations between NATO or the US and terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you can at least agree with that, Mr. Bushi, is that not a single member of your organisation put his signature to the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true, because they were not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you remember that I asked you a number of questions about Ali Ahmeti, your leader, and a number of other leaders of your group, and the measures that had been taken against them, in particular, travel bans and freezing of assets. Do you recall me asking you those questions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well and I said that this was at the beginning of the war and to the end of the war. But now, Mr. -- Mr. Ahmeti travels all around the world, whereas Mr. Thaci has not been anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree that the measures which were --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is still on the black list. Mr. Thaci is still on the black list.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that the basis for the measures which were taken at the time against Ali Ahmeti and other members of your organisation was because they were the leaders of a terrorist or extremist organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree that they were leaders of an extremist organisation. They were leaders of a regular army of the National Liberation Army, and the sanctions were set at the start of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D117.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to show you, and again I apologise there is no Macedonian or Albanian translation of that document. But what I'm about to show you is a so-called presidential executive order, numbered 13219, dated June 26 of 2001. And it is adopted by the president of the United States at the time, President George Bush. I will read out to you what this document says. It says -- the title is blocking property of persons who threaten international stabilization efforts in the Balkans -- in the western Balkans. And it goes on to say that the order is adopted by the authority of the president. And it says this: "I, George W. Bush, president of the United States of America, have determined that the actions of persons engaged in or assisting, sponsoring or supporting, one, extremist violence in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, southern Serbia, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and elsewhere in the western Balkans." And then further down he explained that the person designated by the secretary of the treasury -- that would be -- further down on the page, please. "In consultation with the secretary of state because they are found: (A) to have committed or to pose a significant risk of committing acts of violence that have the purpose or effect of threatening the peace in or diminishing the stability or security of any area or state in the western Balkans region, undermining the authority, efforts or objectives of international organisations or entities present in the region or endangering the safety of persons participating in or providing support to the activities of those international organisations or entities. Or," and then (B) is irrelevant. "Materially to assist in, sponsor or provide financial or technological support for or goods or services in support of such acts or violence or obstructionism; or to be owned or controlled by or acting or purporting to act directly or indirectly for or on behalf of any of the foregoing persons that are --"

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "-- or hereafter, come within the United States or that are or hereafter come within the possession or control of the United States, persons, are blocked and may not be transferred, paid, exported withdrawn or otherwise dealt in." And if we could turn to -- two page further down. It would be 1D00-1578, please. Then, Mr. Bushi, there is the list of person who is are concerned by there presidential order from George Bush and it starts with Mr. Xhevat Ademi, a member of the NLA. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's Mr. Ali Ahmeti, again, NLA. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Nuri Rexhiti of the NLA. Is that someone you know as well?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard him, but I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you go down the list a little bit, there's a man called Hasan or Hasan Xhavit, NLA. That man was your so-called officer for morale, isn't it, Mr. Bushi, the man who you say was in charge of morale in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you go down the list -- if you go down the list there is also Mr. Ostreni Gezim. Do you see him?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And another member of the NLA called Hisni Shaqiri. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Veliu, the -- one of the political leaders of your movement is also mentioned there. Do you see him?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the list of organisation, your organisation, the so-called National Liberation Army, NLA, or UCK is also mentioned on this document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you will agree that at least as far as the United States is concerned, still on the 26th of June of 2001, your organisation and its leaders were regarded as extremists which were destabilising the western Balkans. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I said earlier and repeat it again. This was up until the end of the war, on the 26th of September, 2001. Today, Mr. Ahmeti and Mr. Ostreni, they travelled all around the world, including the United States and Europe and they're not on the black list. I will say it again, Mr. Thaci, Mr. Matoshi, they are still on the black list.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if we can stay, Mr. Bushi, with the year 2001 at this stage. You will agree that as you mentioned all through the, what you call the war, your organisation and its leaders were regarded as terrorists or extremists by the international community. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that was the case at the start of the war, because that's how the Macedonian government, the police and the army introduced us, but at the end of the war, politics changed, everything changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you could tell me this, do you consider the 26th of June of 2001 to be the beginning of the war, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that the beginning, but I wouldn't have said the end either.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that on the day when this -- or a day later rather when this presidential order was issued by President George Bush a press statement was issued by the White House to explain the purpose of this document. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D715, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, the document is a statement of the press secretary of the White House on behalf the president of the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Rule 65 ter 1D715, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, while we're waiting for the document to appear on your screen, I will read it out to you. It is dated the 27 of June of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the registry, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The White House said this: "The United States has joined with its European allies and other countries of the United Nations in strongly condemning the terrorist violence perpetrated by armed extremists determined to destabilize the democratic multi-ethnic government of Macedonia. Their violent tactics threatened US and international efforts to promote regional peace and stability and pose a potential danger to US military forces and other Americans supporting peace keeping efforts. "Macedonian President Trajkovski has asked for our support to combat these extremists who are undermining the political dialogue currently under way among Macedonia's legitimately elected leaders. This dialogue offers a real opportunity for a negotiated and peaceful settlement. As the president stated in Europe, we must face down extremists in Macedonia and elsewhere who seek to use violence to redraw borders and subvert the democratic process." So you will agree, sir, that -- I'm not talking about the beginning of what you call the war, but on the 27th of June, of 2001, the United States was pretty clear that it considered your organisation and the leaders of that organisation to be an extremist organisation that was a destabilizing factor in the democratic Republic of Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, this is not the beginning, nor the end. I know that upon signing of the Ohrid Agreement, on the agreement, on that particular agreement the word terrorist does not appear. And that was on the 13th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the next two paragraph, Mr. Bushi, the document discussed the measures, the particular measures that are adopted in the presidential order that I have discussed with you beforehand, and I don't wish to read that to you. But I'll go to the last-but-one paragraph where the document states that the purpose of the actions taken by the president of the United States and it says this: "The purpose of these two actions is to send a clear message to the extremists and their supporters in the region who actively obstruct and undermine peace and stability, that such tactics are unacceptable and that we will use the means at our disposal to isolate these groups and individuals and cut their access to financial support". And it goes on to say this: "For the first time in history, we have democratic government throughout south-east Europe. Legitimate grievances must be addressed through the democratic process. As President Trajkovski said on Tuesday, Macedonians must reinvigorate the political dialogue with all legitimate parties; the men of violence must lay down their weapons so that all Macedonian citizens can live in peace." Mr. Bushi, were you aware of those calls by the president of the United States that you and your organisation should lay down your arms to give peace a chance in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were aware. I'd like to add some things. In the Macedonian parliament, an amnesty was passed related to the NLA fighters. Tell me if in any country of the world terrorists are being amnestied.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I can ask you is this, Mr. Bushi, did you benefit from the amnesty?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what aspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, did you receive a guarantee from the Macedonian state that you would not be prosecuted for your criminal activities during the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware also, Mr. Bushi, that the European Union adopted similar measures, similar restrictions on the travel and assets of your leaders, the leaders of your group?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know but as far as I know, today from 2001, upon the end of the war in 2001, and the -- the parliamentary elections taking place then, all the former leaders of the NLA can freely travel around the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But would you agree that still in the middle of July of 2001 and thereafter, the European Union considered you and the leaders of your group to be extremists. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that they were referring to you as an extremist organisation and your leaders as extremists. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the end of the war, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will simply show you the document in question so that you can see if it correspond to your memory of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Rule 65 ter 1D118. Has an ERN of 1D00-1580.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, again, this is a document in English only. This is the record of a meeting of the EU council at Brussels on July 16 to 17, 2001. It is an extract on south-east Europe. And if I can draw your attention on the second paragraph of that document, it says this: "The council adopted a common position (see annex 1) banning the issue of visas to extremists, which will be implemented in due course by a subsequent decision on the basis of a recommendation by high representative Javier Solana. The council reiterate on this occasion its condemnation of all forms of extremism in the region." Does that accord with your memory, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we turn to page 1D00-1584, please. Mr. Bushi, this is the actual annex of the same document which was referred to in first paragraph and it contains the council common position of 2001 concerning a visa ban against extremists in the Federal Republic of Macedonia, and I will read out to you the conclusions drawn by the council. It says this: "In its conclusions of 11 June 2001, the council expressed its growing certain at the serious deterioration of the security situation in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, and condemned the continued terrorist actions by ethnic Albanian extremists." So just stopping there for a moment, isn't that the case Mr. Bushi, that the EU, just like the United States was calling you in the alternative, extremists or terrorists or in any case referred to your actions as terrorist acts or terrorist actions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have said terrorist actions. War was still going on. When these conclusions were adopted and I -- I said it and I'll say it again. All the leaders of the KLA from 2002 onwards, they travel freely around the world and they have no obstacles on the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In conditions to or conclusion to, I should say, the EU council said this: "In its conclusions of 25 June 2001, the council continued to condemn all forms of terrorism in the western Balkan region and remain committed to preventing such action from undermining the democratic process, including through restrictive measures such as a visa ban against extremists." And then it says: "No visa should be issued to extremists endangering peace and stability in the Federal Republic of Macedonia and threatening the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Macedonia. And then the council also take notes of the fact that the EU considers the alignment of the central and eastern European countries associated with the EU, the associated countries Cyprus, Malta and Turkey and EFTA countries members of the European economic area to be important in order to maximise the impact of this common position." So you will agree, sir, that at least on the 16 and 17 or still on the 16 and 17 of July of 2001, the EU and associated countries still referred to your organisation as extremists that had recourse to terrorist actions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have said terrorist actions. And all this was up until the signing of the Ohrid Agreement. Sir, today, in 2007, General Stojkovski can still not have Visas to travel the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also that --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was commander of the Lions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also that I asked you a few questions about measures adopted not at the international but at the national level by a number of states in relation to activities by members of your organisation, and I think I mentioned Switzerland, and in response you said that such things did not happen. It is page 5799. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Repeat that again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that last week in the course of my questioning, I asked you a number of questions about measures adopted at the national level, and I think I mentioned Switzerland in particular, that had taken measures against leaders of your organisation. Do you recall me asking you those questions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall suggesting that no such things happened?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D774, please. It is ERN 1D00-7009. There is a German version at 1D00-7008, which is the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours. Sorry to interrupt. Sorry to interrupt but the Defence has provided to the Prosecution three different lists of documents to be used during cross-examination, and at least the last four document that have been used have not been provided to the Defence and we have not been informed. And I will kindly request to the Defence, please, to provide us with a final list of all the documents that they are going use in cross-examination. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise to my colleague. She seems to be correct about those documents, Your Honour. They were not planned to be use this with this witness. It was in view of the answers of the witness last week that we have added them in the course of the weekend. If it is a problem, Your Honour, I could move on from this particular document and come back to it after the break so that we can give a copy to Ms. Regue if she --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be, but the bigger problem is whether there are further documents that have not been the subject of notification.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We believe not too, Your Honour. We will verify that at the break but believe those were the part of the section which related to the answers of Mr. Bushi of last week which led to additional documents being placed. But we will verify that at the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks Your Honour. Just for the record, we have been requesting the Defence from Friday and this morning for additional documents, so they had the time during the weekend to provide us. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, there seems have been some failure of organisation and courtesy. Well, we can hope that won't --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We can consider it the failure of organisation. It was not a matter of lack of courtesy and we hope not and we will certainly provide the copy of the document to Ms. Regue. And as I mentioned, if Ms. Regue feels that this line of questioning or the absence of documents creates any problem for the Prosecution, we could move on to a different subject and come back to the document after the break. But I believe from the line of questioning, Your Honour, that the issues had been properly identified with the witness in the course of last week. And we believe that as far as the subject matter of the issues are concerned, it was identified and also several other documents which related to this issue had been provided to Ms. Regue. We apologise for the fact that some others which were later added have not been and, as I mention, we will provide a copy of this document during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue, is there a reason that you would favour Mr. Mettraux moving to another document at the moment or do you see that as unnecessary?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no problem that he goes on, but it is not a matter of one document so far, it has been a matter of, as I mentioned, four documents this morning. And also every time there is a new document we are asking about that, so we just want to know the final list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mettraux tells us you now have the final list; there are no additional documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, the document that is in front of you -- I will ask the registry to bring up the English version, please. That would be 1D00-7009. Mr. Bushi, while the document is being looked for, this is a press release of sorts from the ministry of justice and police from Switzerland. It is dated the 3rd of July 2001, and it concerns the federal council orders further measures against activists of the Macedonian conflict. Mr. Bushi, the federal council in Switzerland is our government. And the document says this: "On Tuesday, the federal council ordered that measures be implemented against more activists in the Macedonian conflict in Switzerland. Pursuant to Article 184, paragraph 3 of the federal constitution it has banned Ali Ahmeti and Xhavit Haliti from entering Swiss territory without express authorisation until further notice. In addition, it has banned these two persons and Musa Xhaferi from establishing, representing or supporting any organizations which are either directly involved in violent conflict in Macedonia or which indirectly support any of the violent parties. "In case of a breach of these measures, Musa Xhaferi has been threatened with expulsion." And then if go you down two paragraph, it says: "These measures are justified as these three persons occupy leading position in the conflict area and in Switzerland in the KLA and the LPK, popular movement of Kosovo, political extension of the KLA while enjoying regular immigration status in Switzerland." And if you go down further on this page, there's a paragraph starting with the words on 15 June 2001. It says this: "On 15 June 2001, the federal council felt it was necessary to ban the Macedonian national of Albanian ethnicity Fazil Veliu from engaging in any kind of political activity in Switzerland." And just for the record, Fazil Veliu was one of the so-called political leaders of your organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "The explanation for the decision was that Switzerland does not allow the interior security of other states to be directly or indirectly jeopardized from within its own territory. Furthermore, it continues it should not be permissible for any party to a conflict to be actively engaged in a violent confrontation and be able to return to Switzerland at any point." Mr. Bushi, were you aware of those measures taken against various members of your organisation, including Ali Ahmeti and Fazli Veliu who were on Swiss territory at some stage?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These measures were effective up until the end of the war and the signing of the Ohrid Agreement. I'll say it again: The same people today or from 2002 onwards, they go to Switzerland and they travel around Europe and the world. You are talking about the wartime and it was normal at the time to be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the situation this: At the time, Mr. Bushi, your organisation was desperate to receive some degree of political legitimacy and you tried to do so by pretending to be an army. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. When we were fighting we were not a political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, at the time you were a terrorist or an extremist organisation, Mr. Bushi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. We were not terrorists. We were a regular army. Terrorists do not have an emblem, they do not have a uniform, they do not have a rule book. We had all these.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your attempt to get some legitimacy for your movement continue up to this day. Is that correct, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have the legitimacy of the people, sir. We have taken part in democratic elections and we have gained the legitimacy of the people. That's of utmost importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this need for legitimacy, Mr. Bushi, explain that are you not willing and not ready to admit the role and responsibility of your organisation in the commission of crimes such as Ljubotenski Bacila, or your involvement in the event at Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it also explain your unwillingness to disclose the internal functioning of your organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What internal functioning are you talking about? I don't understand that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Bushi, is that in your evidence you've made a number of statements about the alleged organising and structure of your organisation which have as a purpose to create an appearance of an army and without the appearance of a legitimate body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that it was an army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the ways in which you have sought to give a degree of legitimacy to your organisation and you've done it in evidence again here, was to pretend to be complying with the laws of war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that we complied with the laws of war. And the very fact that in Karadak where one soldier, one civilian or two civilians were arrested and subsequently released and not killed is a proof of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you must also be aware, Mr. Bushi, that all those who were kidnapped by your organisation and were never released and are now dead. Do you know about them?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. I know that there are abducted people, but it is not known who abducted them. There are both Albanians and Macedonians kidnapped and time will tell who has carried out these acts. Metush Ajeti was taken from his house and he was killed in the Avtokomanda police station in Skopje. We have Ruzhdi Veliu and his whereabouts remain unknown; we have Sulthan Mehmeti, we have Hani from Veleshta and many others who were taken by uniformed members of the Macedonian police. As for other civilians of Macedonian ethnicity, we heard about those cases from the media but we really don't know who kidnapped them. If you have facts about the individuals who kidnapped them, then you should point them out to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you will agree, I hope that your organisation, you must know, Mr. Bushi, that your organisation committed many crimes and atrocities during the crisis in 2001. That you must know.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true, sir. We did not carry out any crimes. I only ask you to give me as one fact, one single fact, nothing else. Do you know, sir, that when a Macedonian soldier was married, he publicly invited NLA members to his wedding. Do you know this? And this was only due to the fact that we saved his life at that time. We released him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D16, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a document received from the Office of the Prosecutor and it originates from the OSCE spillover monitor mission in Skopje. It appears to be an e-mail sent by the OSCE to Ambassador Stoudman at the time and it records a number of criminal activities by the NLA and I would like to go through this document with you. The author of this document, a person called Eileen Simpson who is a human dimension officer for the OSCE indicates in the e-mail that she is working on a supplemental -- on a supplemental report that will address recent developments. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, to interrupt. But we have not been informed that this document will be used, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Ms. Regue seems to be correct again. This is a document that is already in evidence as an exhibit. But if Your Honour wishes us to comply with what we had mistakenly said before and verify if there is any other documents which have been added which the Prosecution hasn't received, as I indicated the subject the matter of these issues was raised last week we believe that this document had been identified But we can certainly go through the list, Your Honour, right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we will break now to give you an opportunity to do that, Mr. Mettraux, and we will continue at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mettraux, have we got to the bottom of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. And we would wish to apologise to Ms. Regue. She was quite right about the fact that, in fact, the documents that we selected during the weekend by counsel and it is, I should insist, the fault of counsel only mine, were not disclosed before the start of the session this morning. And we apologise to Ms. Regue for any convenience this may have cause. We believe now that all of them have been identified. We went through the list of documents. We believe they have all been identified and provided to Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Ms. Regue, if have you ongoing problems, because of lack of notice, you will let us know.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, if you could look at the document, 1D16, please, on your screen. As I indicated to you, Mr. Bushi, before the break, this is a document from the OSCE organisation prepared by a person Eileen Simpson and it's been sent to Ambassador Stoudmann, and it refers to a supplemental report which this person is preparing concerning human rights violations by the ethnic Albanian armed group and it lists a number of crimes committed by your organisation. The first type of crimes is illegal detentions of civilians. Mr. Bushi, are aware of any such instances, members of your organisation detaining civilians?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware and what you're saying is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The second type of crimes listed by the OSCE are cases of forced labour. Are you aware of any cases of your organisation, the NLA, forcing other persons to work, including ethnic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of such cases, and I don't think such cases were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of cases of forced conscription of ethnic Albanian into your organisation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. As I said earlier, they joined on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of cases of use of juveniles in military operation or within an area of engagement by your organisation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of cases of physical abuse and intimidation of civilians at NLA check-points, including the beating of women and children -- I'm sorry, the beating of men and the intimidation of men and of women and children. Are you aware of such cases?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not and there were no such cases. These things were committed by Macedonian forces and I illustrated this with the case of a father and a son, who were killed for no reason near the stadium. They had no weapon, no uniforms whatsoever on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of a campaign of ethnic cleansing by your organisation to clean areas of non-ethnic Albanian citizens?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that and we did not commit that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of incidents of looting and wanton destruction of property by members of your organisation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not do such things. It was the Lions who did such things even in Macedonian areas and I mentioned the example of Manastir or Bitola.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware that your organisation was using mines to blow up military and police convoys? Are you aware of such incidents?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware that during the crisis in 2001, only you, the NLA, were using mines?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is it not true. It is not true that only the NLA used mines. Also the Macedonian police and army had mines at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if the OSCE were to state that the ethnic Albanian armed group is the only warring party known to have used mines at all, is using anti-tank mines routinely and is suspected of also having placed anti-personnel mines, that would be incorrect, according to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of cases where the NLA initiated hostilities in areas known to be inhabited by civilians. Are you aware of such cases?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, are you aware that your organisation, the NLA, committed murders of armed -- unarmed civilians. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall telling this Chamber that the area around Matejce was within your zone of responsibility, the zone of responsibility of your so-called brigade. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Matejce was not in the area of responsibility 114th Brigade but of 113rd Brigade. Between Matejce and Vistica there was the boundary between the brigades, while Matejce was the area of responsibility and operations of 113rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll just read to you, two passages from your own statement, Mr. Bushi. That is Rule 65 ter 1D830 at page 3 of the document. I'll read it out to you. At paragraph 13, 1-3, it says: "The 114th Brigade maintained observation posts in Orlance, Mojance and Grusino. The front line that the 114th Brigade held ran from Nikustak to Vistica up to Matejce. From Matejce up north --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Matejce of Manastir, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you will agree that the monastery, the areas of Matejce where the monastery was located was under the control of your brigade. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you must have been aware of crimes of mistreatment and kidnapping of civilians which happened in that general area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I already told you there were no abductions and mistreatment. I mentioned the case of the soldier of the ARM, and two civilians who were arrested by us and who were our hostages were subsequently released.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that your leaders, Mr. Ahmeti and Mr. Gezim Ostreni and others were charged in Macedonia in relation inter alia to crimes committed against civilians within the zone of responsibility, which included Matejce. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From which area?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: From various areas, Mr. Bushi, including the Matejce area. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. Such an indictment was not issued by the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, Mr. Bushi, that those accusations raised against Mr. Ahmeti and Gezim Ostreni which had led to some activities in Macedonia were later taken over by the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware, but to my knowledge, the Tribunal did not recognise these facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Exhibit P391. Your Honour, this is the Prosecution's request for deferral. And I would ask the registry to go to page N000-9883-15. That's an annex to this document. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, there is no Albanian translation of this document, so I will have to read it out to you. It's a letter signed by Madam Del Ponte, the Chief Prosecutor of the ICTY. It is sent to Mr. Stavre Dzikov, public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia. It is dated the 26th of April of 2002. I believe you now have a Macedonian version in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask the registry to turn to the second page of this document, please, of the next page. And to focus, first on the second paragraph, please. Mr. Bushi, there's a sentence or a paragraph --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it in the Macedonian version before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the second page of the document be shown in Macedonian as well, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, if you look for a paragraph that in the English starts with the words: "As stated already, the NLA leadership case." Can you find that? I believe it is the second paragraph on your page as well?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read it out to you. It says this: "As already noted, the 'NLA leadership case' is being investigated by my office and this investigation is still ongoing. Evidence linking the NLA leadership to the incidents in Matejce and Lipkovac will be important and I seek your assistance in providing such evidence." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to now read not the next paragraph but the one after. It says this: "In providing this opinion, it must be stressed that this conclusion does not suggest that the allegations nor the facts that the crimes were committed are in dispute. It does mean, however, that without more information concerning the crimes and relevant evidence linking the suspects to those crimes, my office is not in a position to assess the case conclusively or to make a final decision at this moment." So you will agree, Mr. Bushi, at least based on this document that as far as the Office of the Prosecution was concerned, they did not have any doubt that crimes had been committed in Matejce. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. If they had any doubts that Mr. Ostreni and Mr. Ahmeti committed crimes, they would have been arrested and now in the detention centre in Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that true, Mr. Bushi also that the reason why you claimed in your statement and repeated here in evidence that your organisation was respecting religious and culture site was for the same reason, to give an appearance of legitimacy to your organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that we respected these facilities and not for the purpose of appearance of legitimacy but this was in line with the rules of the NLA and the order from the General Staff. That is not to touch any religious facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth that you paid no attention any such documents and that you in fact used and targeted religious and cultural monuments, be they Orthodox or Muslim. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. We did not aim at any religious building. This is what they did. We can mention here the religious buildings in Haracin, in Matejce, in Nagustak which were targets of the Macedonian police and army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you will recall the evidence or the information provided by some members of your brigade that you were the one who ordered that your organisations or members thereof start shelling the Orthodox church in the village or near the village of Ljuboten. Do you recall that? Do you recall people making such claims?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall what they said but I never issued such an order. If I issued an order to that effect, it would have been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also the case, Mr. Bushi, that within your area of responsibility, so-called, there were a number of mosques that you used as military positions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D807, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, the document that is in front of you is a so-called daily bulletin on non-compliance with the cease-fire and it covers the period from 1800 hours on the 14th of July of 2001 to 0600 hours on the 15th of July of 2001, and the document was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor and it comes, as you can see, from the bottom left-hand corner of the document from the OSCE archives in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to turn to the second page of that document. That would be 1D00-7140.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In this document, Mr. Bushi, there's a number of entries which concern observation made by various organisations or entities and it is kept in a chronological order. And I would like to read to you the first incident or the first matter recorded in this document. It is recorded at 1830 on the 14th of July of 2001. And the submitting authority is the army, -- that's the army of the Republic of Macedonia and it records the following: "Our positions were watched at 2015 hours on 13 July 2001 from the village of Ropalce at 07.40 at 14 July 2001 from the village Matejce and at 1335 hours from the mosque in the village Nikustak." And just stopping there for a moment, Mr. Bushi, Nikustak was the village in which you had the headquarters of your brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of a church in Nikustak. There was a mosque there but not a church.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bushi, it should have said --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was mosque there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Bushi. The translation must have misled you. The text said: "From the mosque in the village of Nikustak." And I'll ask to you look at the third annotation in this document which is again coming at 1830 on the 14th of July 2001. It says this: "At 1440 hours on 14 July of 2001, several persons were registered working on sandbag trenches by the mosque in the village Nikustak." Mr. Bushi, isn't that correct, that you installed reinforced position just next to the mosque in the village of Nikustak?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mosque. This is not correct. We had our front line from Nikustak in the direction of Vistice, Matejce and Likovc. And this front line had nothing to do with the mosques.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bushi, if I understand you properly, your evidence is that this information about sandbag trenches by the mosque in the village of Nikustak is wrong or false. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say whether there were nearby but there were none in the mosque. The front line was, as I earlier mentioned. This information that you're reading comes from the Macedonian forces. And as I said earlier, all the information coming out from the period from 14th February to 26th of September have no truth in our opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that you reserved your worst treatment and by your, I mean your brigade, your worst treatment for orthodox properties and orthodox religious buildings. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. We had the monastery in Matejce and we did not cause any damage to it or blow it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that after the cease-fire, a cease-fire had been reached with the Macedonian authorities, your brigade conducted destruction in and around the village of Matejce. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period of time are you referring to, sir, and which cease-fire? Of what date?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be the early days of the month of July of 2001, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D817. It has an ERN 1D00-7179.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, before I show you the document, is it your evidence that you are aware of members of your brigade burning houses and damaging churches at any other time during that period, up to the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing of the kind happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is one of the document which was provided by the source which was indicated during the private hearing at the beginning of the evidence of this witness. And I will ask the registry to turn to the third page of that document. It is 1D00-7181. Mr. Bushi, I will read the passage to you from this document which comes from -- originated in an embassy. It says this: "As of 1900 hour, Embassy DAO confirmed that the cease-fire is holding, but there are six major fires burning in the southern (ethnic Macedonian) part of Matejce. And that the orthodox church and what locals report to be a flour mill is burning."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mill, flour mill.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "A flour mill is burning. This DAO observations appear to confirm local reports that the NLA is burning the Macedonian part of Matejce as they depart. The ancient monastery outside of Matejce, however, is not on fire." Mr. Bushi, were you aware of any members or any member of your so-called brigade being involved in burning ethnic Macedonian property and damaging the orthodox church in Matejce?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With full responsibility I say that no member of the brigades 114 and 113 did such things. You should know that that part of the area, Vistica-Matejce was part of the front line and that there was firing on both sides, from our side and from the army's -- Macedonian army's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So it's your evidence, Mr. Bushi, that the information contained in this document is incorrect. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been fire in houses because of the firing, but not that any individuals set fire to the houses deliberately.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bushi, also that upon your withdrawal or the departure of members of your brigade, you and your colleagues destroyed the old Macedonian orthodox monastery outside of Matejce. Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This did not happen. We had control over the monastery. If we wanted to do that, we would have done it. Nobody prevented us from doing that, but we didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware that of the fact that several of your colleagues, several of the people who were members of your organisation were charged with serious criminal offence for their activities in the crisis in 2001, and that those charges include, in particular, the damage done to the monastery in Matejce. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that, but it depends on who is laying the charges and who is putting these accusations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You are aware, Mr. Bushi, that among those accused of being responsible for these crimes are Mr. Veliu, Mr. Ahmeti, Mr. Ostreni, and your so-called chief of morale, Xhavit Hasani. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: May have been accused, but there is no truth in what are you saying, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And how do you suggest, Mr. Bushi, this 14th-century monastery came to be destroyed. What's your evidence on this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the monastery in Matejce?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. The Sveta Bogorodica monastery, a 14th-century monastery in the village of Matejce.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably done by the shelling on the part of police force, on the other side. They never stopped shelling the area which was controlled by us and that carried on 24 hours, non-stop and they used tanks and artillery to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that your evidence that the same explanation explained that the old monastery in Lesok was also blown up as the NLA was withdrawing. Is that the same things that happened there?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
