utterances.text: -- know anything about the Lesok monastery. But I'm certain that nothing of the kind was carried out by the forces of the KLA -- the NLA, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bushi, that another way in which you pretended to be an army was to pretend that you were wearing uniforms with badges and ranks at -- all the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's accurate that we were a regular army, having all the assets of an army, the emblems, the uniforms, the ranks and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But staying for a minute with the issue of the uniform, Mr. Bushi, is that correct that your organisation, the NLA, would often operate without any uniform. Do you agree with that? Including members of your brigade.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D823, please. It is ERN 1D00-7210.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is again a document in English only, unfortunately. This is a report, spot report on armed activity in the Tanusevci area. It is dated the 6th of March 2001, and the document comes from the OSCE, once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask to you focus, Mr. Bushi, if you can see it on the paragraph starting with the paragraph letter B, the village of Tanusevci. Can you see that? I'll read it out to you. It says this: "The village of Tanusevci has been the scene of a withdrawal northwards of up to 100 of the ethnic Albanian armed group EAAG which had been occupying the area since about the 21st February. The ethnic Albanian armed group members were observed to have moved into the village of Debelde where they appeared to be dressed in normal civilian clothing having abandoned both military style uniforms and weapons." Mr. Bushi, do you agree that this document would suggest, at least as far as your colleagues from the Tanusevci area are concerned, they would, when convenient, shed their uniforms. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that. In Debelde, Debelde is part of Kosova and you couldn't get into that area in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you will agree, Mr. Bushi, then that, when convenient, the members of your organisation would simply take out their uniforms. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D829, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is again the same collection of documents that I've shown you on a couple of occasion last week. Those are information provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by a particular state.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry to go to page 21 of this document. That would be 1D00-7291. If we could have the English version. This would be starting at 1D00 -- yes, I'm grateful. Thank you. That would be the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is a report, Mr. Bushi, that is dated the 16 of August of 2001. And it talks about a particular road known as the Fox route which is in and around the area of Tetovo. And if the registry could move to the next page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In this report, Mr. Bushi, the authorities say this: "In Albanian dominated villages north of Fox route we still observed some NLA fighters who, until recently wore their uniforms but were now in civilian clothes.'? Would you agree that it also happened that NLA members, not only in Tanusevci but also in Tetovo and other places were taking off their uniforms when they saw fit. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that. And that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree or can you recall when your colleague and member of your brigade, the nickname Teli was killed? Do you remember the date when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that. On the 7th of August, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that he was killed in the centre of the capital, Skopje, in the Gazi Baba neighbourhood. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, Mr. Bushi, that your colleague Mr. Teli who went to the city to conduct terrorist activities was wearing his uniform at the time?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a terrorist activity. It was an observation unit, and I don't know how he was killed, but they were carrying weapons and uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that he would walk in the middle of Skopje wearing his NLA uniform, Mr. Bushi, carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that he was walking in the middle of Skopje. But when he left the village, he had the uniform and he had the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you think that he was still wearing this uniform and carrying his weapon when he arrived in the area of Gazi Baba?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normal that the Skopje area was part of our activity and he couldn't have walked in uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, it was not part of our activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bushi, if Skopje is not part of your activities, what was Mr. Teli doing in town?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was part of a reconnaissance team.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Isn't that correct that you gave yourself names, titles, and ranks, but in practice, they meant little or nothing. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree that we gave ourselves ranks, but that was as part of a military set-up, according to the rule book we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bushi, that you were a member of the JNA, the Yugoslav Army, for five years from 1987 to 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in those five years, you reached the rank of Sergeant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was senior high-ranking military man.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you remember the title that you had in the JNA, your rank?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: B sergeant [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you then spent the next ten years -- nine or ten years, from 1992 to 2001 in the Macedonian army?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you say what rank you reached during these nine years in the Macedonian army?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Senior Sergeant first class.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And by comparison, is it correct that in the so-called NLA, you were at once given the rank of Colonel by Gezim Ostreni. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in line with the military structure of our army, I -- I deserved to have the title of a brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about your chief -- so-called chief of operations Mr. Ramadan Limaj. What was his rank at the time?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was lieutenant-colonel, in line with the military structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what military experience did Mr. Limaj have prior to the crisis?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the crisis he was involved in the Kosovo conflict and he had graduated from an academy. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know what his profession was before the crisis?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The ranks in the NLA were given in line with the rule book of the NLA. Whoever came, all the titles, the ranks, the operational chiefs or others, they were granted these ranks in line with the operational structure of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that the military experience or lack thereof would be not be relevant to the distribution of those names and titles. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you, because all those who were in the operational staff of the 114th Brigade they had experience, relevant experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war in Presevo, Kosovo. And from their military background.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about your so-called officer for morale, Mr. Xhavit Hasani. What was his rank in your organisation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was captain of first class. Major.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall what Mr. Hasani's occupation was before the war?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war? Before the war, he worked in forestry. As far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he did there. But he was involved in forestry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know now where Mr. Xhavit Hasani is, your chief of morale?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is in the prison of Dubrave.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: He is in the prison in Kosovo for murder and other terrorist activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not accurate. He has been charged on the basis of allegations coming from Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The charges come from Macedonia because the crimes were committed in Macedonia but he hasn't just been charged; he has been convicted and sentenced to 13 years in prison. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not accurate, sir. There are facts that you may be able to find in Kosovo and Macedonia. He was charged by Macedonia for actions, acts committed in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: He is in prison in Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that -- well, you will recall being shown a number of badges or insignias by my colleague which was said to relate to the NLA. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that those two didn't mean much. They were just for the show. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. It wasn't for a show, but it was a reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bushi, that, for instance, you, as a so-called colonel of the NLA, never wore those patches on your uniform. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes I carried them; sometimes, I didn't; but most of the time I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is 1D905. This is ERN 1D00-7768.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is the proofing notes that the Prosecution gave to us a few days ago. I will actually read it to you, I don't know it is necessary, but ... The Prosecutor asked you a number of questions about uniforms and ranks. And what you told the Prosecution was: "My rank was colonel general, but I never wore the patch indicating my rank." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, and as I said, most of the time I didn't wear that, and sometimes I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Page 5 for the registry, it is page 1D00-7772. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But when you were asked by the Prosecution during your proofing session you told them: "My rank was colonel general but I never wore the patch indicating my rank." Is that correct? That's what you told them then.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes, as I said, I did wear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the -- your evidence is that the Prosecution misunderstood what you had told them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there was some misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it earlier, that most of the time I did not carry the rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, sir, that your so-called brigade was in fact just a loose group of individuals dressed up, for the most part, as fighters. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that it took you only between two or three days to set up or to form the 114th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That that's not correct. It was two to three days to set up the staff, but mobilisation continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, since the document is on the screen. It is again your proofing notes, Mr. Bushi, and I will ask to you look a bit further down the dots. There's a comment attributed to you by the Office of the Prosecutor where it says: "It took two, three days to form the 114th Brigade." Are you suggesting again that the --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the brigade staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you're suggesting again that the person who took down your statement misunderstood what you said. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that, Mr. Bushi, your brigade never looked anything like the regulations which had been prepared, drafted within your organisations?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, Mr. Bushi, that those regulation just like many of the other things you did or pretended to do at the time, were just intended to give the appearance of legitimacy to your organisation and to make it look like a valid military organisation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct that we did that for that aim. The NLA was a regular army and we had to respect all the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the rules mention, among other things, that the brigade should have a lengthy part concerning your legal advisor and among other thing your press information centre. I suppose you will recall that when I asked about this, you told me that you had no legal advisor at the time and that there was no press information centre in your brigade. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the information centre was shared between the 114 and 113 brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, that when I asked you whether your brigade had such an organ you told me, no, that is not the case. That's page 5646. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have an information centre in our brigade but it was shared by the two brigades in the Karadak region. But it was both the brigades, the 113rd and the 114th which shared the information centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that, to make it look like the NLA was more serious and a bigger organisation than it was, you also invented non-existent brigades. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct, what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, for instance, that the so-called 111 Brigade which appears on some of the NLA documents, in fact was never activated, it had no barracks and no HQ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not accurate. It had everything, the soldiers and the barracks and the HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber, perhaps, where that barracks and this HQ were based?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Staff of the 114th Brigade was in Lustak, whereas of the 1st Battalion were -- was in Nagustak. The 2nd Battalion was in the monastery in Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that last week, Mr. Bushi, you indicated that although this brigade was functional it was, in fact, never activated. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said referred to 111st brigade which was in a state of readiness, whereas the 114th Brigade, it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, in that case we have been misunderstanding each other. I was talking of the 111 brigade. So do you agree that this brigade was never activated. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also the case of the 117?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But to my knowledge, the 117th Brigade did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, is that correct that another way in which you exaggerated the danger posed by your organisation was by inflating the numbers of alleged members of your brigade. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that we inflated the number artificially, but we did this because of the needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that you said that you had 1.000 members within your so-called brigade but that in fact, you had between 200 and 250 men. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the transcript I intended to say between 200 and 250. It is at page 59, line 22. You remember, Mr. Bushi, being shown some documents, tables which recorded, they were model regulations which recorded membership in two particular brigades. Do you recall being shown this document?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you indicated that you kept similar types of records for your brigade. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Have you been able to give copies of those records to the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I handed over the archives of my brigade to the General Staff of the NLA at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you know where those archives are at present, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that the General Gezim Ostreni can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Prosecution Exhibit P321, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'd like to show you a document. It is entitled Macedonia briefing pack. And you will recall it was shown to you during proofing session. Do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask the registry to turn to page R0376858 in the English. And the Macedonian would be R3037-6858-MF.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you remember being shown this particular table during your meeting with the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall being asked whether these charts or documents accurately reflected the structure of your organisation at the time. Do you recall being asked those questions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall making a number of comments, pointing to inaccuracies in this and other documents. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the comments you made at the time was that the 111 had never been activated and that the 117 never came in existence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page after that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recall being shown this document as well? This is the next page of this same document and again being asked certain questions about the accuracy or otherwise of this document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall what corrections, so to say, you made to that particular scheme?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you tell this Chamber, please, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said as far as Melam Fazliu [phoen] is concerned, he was not there. Emrual Shini [phoen], Emrush Xhemali and Dreni, who is said here to be an assistant, he was not an assistant, he was a person responsible for technical issues and informations. As for Ilir, last name unknown, it should be Nazmi Beqir, aka, Iliri. As for the remaining two, Musa Xhaferi --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the second name.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- they were there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Bushi. You've mentioned two individuals who were in the NLA political leadership and I believe the interpreter picked up Musa Xhaferi but not the other person. Could you repeat the name of that person, please?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Isni Shaqiri and Musa Xhaferi.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it also correct that you pointed out to the Office of the Prosecutor that the other three individuals at the bottom of this page, Milajm Fazu, Emrala Uksini, and Emrush Xhemali were not within the NLA political leadership as indicated in this document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page of this document, both in English and in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you remember being shown this document and being asked again to make some comments about the structure presented here. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate what corrections you suggested should be made to that document.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following corrections. I said that I don't know Avni Dehari and Baskim Ramadani. Here where it says advisor Avni Dehari, I said that it could be Fatmir Dehari, not Avni Dehari. As for Isa Demiri [phoen], I said yes, he was; Dreni, yes; Nazmi Baqiri, yes; as well as, Shefet, aka Kravata.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall being shown this document as well, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall making a number of corrections or ...

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not sure if you can enlarge it, please. Now it's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you indicate what's wrong with this diagram.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 113rd Brigade commander was not Ibrahim but Sami Uksini, aka Sokoli. The commander of 112nd Brigade used to be Hasbi Lika, not Kagurrela, and in the meantime when Hasbi Lika was transferred to the General Staff, he was replaced by Isa Lika, aka Iliri. Xhavit Hasani was not in the General Staff of the NLA but was a member of the staff of the 114th Brigade, he was an officer of morale and information. And here Ibrahim Dehari again appears, I said I did not hear of this person; it could be Fatmir Dehari. And another correction was that before Sami Uksini, Sokoli, it was Fadilja Nemani, aka Tigri, who was killed in Vaksince, and later on he was replaced by Sami. Then Refez Halili is stated here; his last name should be Haliti. And then another correction, it says Hasan, it should be Nazim. As for Tala Xhaferi, it's fine. Then another Zaki is mentioned here. I don't know about this person. And as I said, about the 111st brigade, it was in a state of readiness; and the 117, it did not exist. These were the corrections that I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Bushi. You would agree that this particular chart and the others that I have shown you earlier contained quite a number of mistakes and inaccuracies. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record this document was presented and apparently prepared in part, you will recall by the witness Mr. Hutch, and the discussion as to the reliability of this document or otherwise was discussed on the 28th of June of 2007, at page 2809, 2835, and the objection of the Defence was at 2831.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Bushi, that another way in which your organisation sought to have or to obtain some degree of legitimacy was by issuing a number of so-called communiques coming from Mr. Ahmeti or other members of this organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. The communiques were issued by Mr. Ahmeti for one reason: To give a fair picture and to avoid any manipulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you believe -- do you remember, Mr. Bushi, expressing the view that you believed that Mr. Boskoski had been supporting or requesting that the Macedonian state should declare a state of war in Macedonia. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you based those -- this belief on media reports. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on media information and use.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were not privy to any discussion within the Macedonian government about this matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you, based on the information we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, being shown the book that was written by Mr. Boskoski. Do you recall being shown this book by my colleague?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown what is Exhibit P402.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'm again going to show you the same section of the book as was shown you to, a different passage. It is at page 31 of the book. This would be N000-N607-ET-31. Mr. Bushi, the passage which I would wish to read to you is at the top of the page. It starts with the word: "After the proposals." I will read it out to you. It says this: "After the proposals by Prime Minister Ljupco Georgievski, presented to the public in a few occasions for rapid resolve of the crisis in Macedonia by declaring a state of war, which was opposed by the community of ethnic Albanians in our country, because the leaders were under pressure of the powerful Albanian lobby abroad, which was actually drawing the strings for destroying the sovereign Macedonian state. The proposal for declaring state of war was also rejected by the president of the state Boris Trajkovski who was to sign the possible decision on it. Sir, based on the passage that I've read to you, do you agree that the suggestion or proposal that had been made to declare a state of war in the country was made, in fact, by the then prime minister Mr. Ljupco Georgievski and that it was opposed by the then President Trajkovski who was the authority permitted to make such a declaration. Do you agree that's what the book suggests?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the book says, but that's not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know, Mr. Bushi, under Macedonian law what authority is competent to declare a state of war? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know what legal, practical and constitutional consequences this would have had in Macedonia or is it something that is beyond your domain of knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a certain knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that this would have allowed the government to rule, among other things, by decree. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But it never happened. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'd like to turn to something slightly different, another part of your evidence which you've given to the Office of the Prosecutor and that concerns the incident in Ljubotenski Bacila. Do you recall being asked a number of questions by the Prosecution in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall telling the Prosecution in response to a question that you had nothing to do with the incident and that your brigade could not have been involved without your knowledge. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall suggesting to the Office of the Prosecutor that it was not the NLA that had conducted this attack but that in fact it had been Mr. Boskoski who had organised the whole thing. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting it to you, Mr. Bushi, that, in fact, the incident at Ljubotenski Bacila was organised by members of your so-called brigade, in particular, members of the so-called Teli unit. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm also putting it to you that you, Mr. Bushi, was the one who ordered the members of your brigade to go to Ljubotenski Bacila and blow up the army convoy. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. I didn't issue any order of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm also putting it to you that once the operation carried out by the members of your unit, several of them withdrew towards and into the village of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D811, please. It is 1D00-7162 for the English and 7160 for the Macedonian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go through this document with you. It's a report about terrorist attack. It's dated the 10th of August of 2001 and it comes from the headquarters of the 3rd Guardist Batallion which is part of the Macedonian army. And it says the following about this incident: "On 10 August 2001 at about 8.00, military vehicle" and then there is the number and so on. "When returning after a shift from the position Zdravec hit an explosive device with rear right tire. The power of the explosion turned the vehicle over and it landed on the roof together with the soldiers it carried. As the vehicle turned over, terrorists who were in ambush on the north-eastern side in the cottages Bacila, belonging to the Ljuboten residents, Vedri, Kadri, and Murati Muharem opened fire from infantry weapons." Then it goes on: "The units that was located at the positions Zdravec returned fire at the terrorists to ensure access and assistance for the injured. At the same time, in coordination with the battalion HQ 120-millimetre mortars and 2.76-millimetre cannons opened fire. After that, the terrorists stopped actions, fire, and withdrew in the direction of Saint Kamen. While a small group, three or four men, withdrew in the direction of Ljuboten. The same group was spotted by our position our posts while entering into one of the two abandoned cottages, Bacila, and B-1 cannons fired 14 rounds at them. One terrorist was seen running above the cottage, Bacilo, in the direction of Kuljm, and the cottage Bacilo was destroyed." And then if you go further down that document, it says that: "During fighting our unit killed four terrorists." And it says that: "Two were killed at the entrance to the village, one was killed above a water source above the village of Ljuboten. He had a horse with saddle packs. The fourth terrorist with a packed mule was killed in the area of the forest above the road that leads to Ljuboten." Mr. Bushi, do you agree that the information contained in this document is true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not accurate and has nothing to do with the reality. And I would kindly ask you to give me the names of what you called terrorists of those four that were killed, if they were killed indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also refer the Chamber to the evidence of Mr. Mario Jurisic, Mr. Despodov and the OSCE report of 10 August 2001, Exhibit 1D13, 1-3 and 1D86. Mr. Bushi, do you know a person called or known as Gasda Ardi.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He lives nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You mean nearby Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nearby by my residence where I live. He lives in Skopje, but by origin he is from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And his real name is Nexhmedin Fazliu, aka Nexha. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nexhmedin Fazliu, Nexha.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have indicated that is he a neighbour of yours in Skopje and he also has shepherd houses above Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those in your language and in the Macedonian language as known as -- are known as Bacino -- Basinec. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basinec, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the men which you had sent to carry out the operation in Ljubotenski Bacila had stayed in one of these Basinec above the village of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, and Nexhmedin was never a member of the NLA. He had nothing to do with the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'm not suggesting that Mr. Fazliu is or is not a member of the NLA. Are aware of the fact that the persons which you had sent to Ljubotenski Bacila to carry out the attack had stayed in one of the Basinec above the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D161, please. It is 1D00-5405. Thank you. And 5403 for the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a document or an information collected by the state security and counterintelligence service, UBK or DBK of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia and it is dated the 15th of August of 2001. And there is a passage which I would like to read to you and it starts in the middle of the page and it starts with, "the source." This will also be the 2nd paragraph in the Macedonian version, Mr. Bushi, and it says the following: "The source said that Albanian terrorists, a group of 25 strong, took care to set the mine on the road. Some of them were from Kosovo, and some from Ljuboten village. The head of the group, the one who organised the operation was Xhavit Hasani who had large support with people with crime dossiers, residents of Ljuboten village." It goes on to say this: "Otherwise, the men who placed the mines had their meeting the night before the incident occurred. Their meeting point were weekend cottages at the location Basinec. Some of the men were staying there already and others from Ljuboten village came to Basinec walking down the brook stream passing by the patrols of the army." That's what happened, isn't it, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The document, Mr. Bushi, continues by saying this: "Afterwards, the most of the terrorist group went in the direction of the ridge of the Kumanovo regions and others went back in Ljuboten village and they got settled there, in houses of the so-called upper neighbourhood." Again, that's what happened, Mr. Bushi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what happened. It did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the document further says that: "Unknown persons had gathered in Ljuboten village prior to the incident, as the source mentioned during the conversation (most possible they were from Kosovo). These men introduced themselves as members of the Xhavit Hasani's group. Small group of them wore black uniforms and others in civilian clothes strolled in the village." Do you agree that's what happened, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you will recall that before the break we were discussing the area above Ljuboten called Basinec. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bushi, that this area had been used by your organisation as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters have lost the sound. They can't hear.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the interpreter hear now?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I apologize. I think we had some technical problems. I will ask you the question once again. Is it correct that the area above the village of Ljuboten called Basinec had been used by your organisation, the NLA, as a logistical facility. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it had been used as such since the month of March of 2001, at the least. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply to save time we indicate for the record, for the transcript Exhibit 1D168 and Exhibit 1D143.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you have told this Trial Chamber that your brigade consisted of approximately one thousand men. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall saying also that your supplies and logistics were coming not from Ljuboten but from the town of Aracinovo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you tell this Chamber how many kilos of food you needed every day or every week for 1.000 men?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat the question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Could you indicate approximately, I'm not asking you for a detailed answer, but approximately how many kilos of food you would need to feed the 1.000 people which you say were members of your organisation at the time. Per day or per week.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but Selam Hasani was the head of logistics; he would know better. And all things like bread was prepared in the village, it was not coming from the city. From the city we brought in other stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree that approximately for each men you would need a supply of about one kilo of food and drinks per day. Is that approximately correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know how many kilos or what quantity of ammunition, mortars, guns and so on you needed for your organisation on a regular basis? Do you know that, for the 1.000 men?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're not measured by kilogram. They are measured by the piece, and weapons we've had, starting from pistols, Kalashnikovs, hand grenades, mortar 62-millimetres, grenade launchers -- we had hand grenade launchers, 150 and 500.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you able to say how many pieces or what quantity of ammunition and materiel you would receive every week or on a monthly basis, whatever you can assess?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the rest of logistics, clothing, medical supplies and so on and so forth. What quantity would you receive on a weekly basis for your brigade?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in accordance with the needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The quantities both of medical supply, clothing, guns, ammunition and so on, they were quite consequent, is that correct? They were quite large, large quantities.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were large quantities and there were people responsible for looking after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell this Chamber how you would transport this logistic, the food, the medical supplies and the ammunition. How would you transport those?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the logistics who was in charge of that and it was done by using horses.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bushi, that it is completely impracticable, and if not completely impossible, for a group of one thousand men to be resupplied from Nikustak to Aracinovo using, as you suggest horses. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with what you're saying. It depends on how good the organisation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Bushi, that at the time the town of Aracinovo had been completely encircled by the Macedonian forces and that your men who were in town at the time were only able to extract themselves from there when a deal was struck between the Macedonian forces and NATO. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was surrounded, but we had our lines of supply. There were ways of going to the monastery in Matejce and through Nagustak.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are suggesting that while your men who were surrounded by Macedonian forces in Aracinovo could not get out of the area, members of your brigade were able, on a daily or weekly basis to go in and out with large quantities of supplies on horses. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way how supplies are brought in is not done in the way you are suggesting. We had our own way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can you explain then how would you bring all of that logistical material back from Aracinovo and how you would go there?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the materials came from Skopje to Haracin and then from there it was taken to Nagustak and to the monastery. We had another supply route, from the 113rd Brigade. That was through Tanusevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that your evidence, Mr. Bushi, that whilst your colleagues who were in the town of Aracinovo encircled by the Macedonian forces could not get out and that it took NATO to trigger a deal you and your people the 114th and the 113rd were able to go back and forth in the city to get supplies out for your troops. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what is correct, Mr. Bushi, is that in fact most of your logistical supply came from the village of Ljuboten. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not at all true. Ljuboten was not important to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage I'd simply record or will refer for the transcript to Exhibit P438 on that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, that you were asked a number of questions by my colleague from the Prosecution and by myself about a person called Baki Halimi. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that I put to you that Baki Halimi was actually acting as your logistic man in Ljuboten and you denied that was the case. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, there's a number of documents that I would like to show to you which have been provided to us by the Office of the Prosecution in the course of last week. The first one is Rule 65 ter 1D877. Mr. Bushi, what will appear in front of you and is now in front of you is an investigator's notes taken by the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal during an interview with a person, a Ljuboten resident called Murseli Hisni. And if you look further down in this document, in particular at point 2, what Mr. Murseli told the Office of the Prosecutor was that when the conflict in Macedonia started, Alimi became a logistical -- a logistics supporter of the NLA. And that's the truth, isn't it, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness then be shown Rule 65 ter 1D876, please..

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And while it appears, Mr. Bushi, I'm putting it to you that you're not willing to tell the truth to this Chamber about the way in which your organisation was organised, in particular how its supply and logistics were organised. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree and I'm telling the truth. And, as I said, supplies were being taken in the way that I described it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the document you have now in front of you, Mr. Bushi, is a -- another investigator's notes, again taken by the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, this time with Mr. Baki Halimi himself. And I'd like to read to you what Mr. Halimi said to the Office of the Prosecutor. It says this: "During the conversation, Mr. Halimi told us that he was affiliated to the NLA and that he supported the NLA. However, stated that he was not an active member of the NLA and he denied that he was a soldier of the NLA. Mr. Halimi said that he supported the NLA with logistical and financial support; that is, that he collected money from villagers of Ljuboten and other ethnic Albanians for the NLA. He described it as 'raising funds.'" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. That's in English, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If one could turn to the next page, please. And I'll draw your attention to the second paragraph in this document. This was a later meeting between the Office of the Prosecutor and Mr. Halimi. And during that meeting Mr. Halimi said this: "Mr. Halimi acknowledges that he sympathized and supported the NLA. He explained that he provided logistical support to the NLA.'. And that's the truth, isn't it, Mr. Bushi, that despite your denial, Mr. Halimi was the one taking care of logistics for you in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Mr. Halimi was not a member of the NLA, and he was not in charge of logistics. He was not a member of the NLA, I repeat. He was a sympathizer of the NLA, providing moral support. And as for what you're saying, financial support, he -- anyone should have had the authorisation from the headquarters, general headquarters of the NLA to conduct that kind of operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or from the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, being asked by the Prosecution whether you could recall what had happened in Ljubotenski Bacila on the 10th of August of 2001, and you told the Prosecution that you had learned about what had happened from Baki Halimi. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the record this is at page 5607, 25th of September of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also being asked by my colleague of the Prosecution whether your brigade had received an order to organise the mine incident in Ljubotenski Bacila, or if you yourself had given such an order and you responded that neither had happened. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is at page 5609, 25th of September, 2007. And you also asked by my colleague whether you knew of the involvement of any of your soldiers in this incident and you said you didn't. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that there was an incident. And I don't know about the involvement of such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you, Mr. Bushi, that you are not telling the truth and that you are, in fact, hiding the role, the responsibility and the functioning of your organisation, the NLA. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, on the 21st of August of 2003, the Office of the Prosecutor talked to a former member of your organisation, the NLA, a man who had been a member of your so-called brigade in -- at the time in August of 2001. And he told the following to the Office of the Prosecutor: "Teli's group planted the mine that killed Macedonian soldiers on the Friday." That would be Friday, the 10th of August. And that's correct, isn't it, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he added the following when talked to the Prosecution: "Teli himself had been killed before the group assumed his name. Bushi ordered to plant the mine on the road on which the Macedonian soldiers used to move. Hodza told Bushi not to plant the mine and said that if the mine was to be planted some NLA element should enter Ljuboten to prevent another Racak from happening. And again, that's the truth, Mr. Bushi, isn't it. You were the one who ordered your men to go to Ljubotenski Bacila to blow up and murder a number of members of the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct. I have never issued such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this man, Hodza who suggested to you that you should not plant this mine or which, to avoid another Racak, that would be Mr. Xhezair Shaqiri. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Xhezair Shaqiri is Hodza, yes. But it is not that he said such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that is the man who you tried to distance yourself in evidence last week saying that this man had nothing to do with your brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact what Mr. Shaqiri didn't understand it was your purpose and that of Mr. Ostreni who had given you an order at the time precisely to create an incident that would trigger a reaction from the Macedonian forces. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. General Ostreni gave no such order. Neither did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will also refer for the transcript to Exhibit 1D167.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, sir, that contrary to your claims of the accusations that you directed at others, in particular at Mr. Boskoski or generally at the Macedonian forces, the representative of the international community had no doubt who had planted the mines in Karpalak on the 8th of August and in Ljubotenski Bacila on the 10th of August and that was the NLA, your organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Ljuboten is concerned, I can say things with full responsibility. But when it comes to Karpalak I cannot say that, because it wasn't under my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown what is Exhibit 1D14, please. And if you could scroll down a little bit in that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a press article, but what I would like to show to you, it is dated the 10th of August of 2001, and it is from the Guardian newspaper. The passage I would like to bring to your attention is the middle of the page and starts with the word: "The US envoy to Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be the sixth paragraph in the document.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in the version that is on the screen, Your, Honour that would be further down the document where it starts with the word: "Speaking in Sofia." This is a slightly different version. I'll use the one that is on the screen. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is a statement attributed to, Mr. Bushi, to Mr. Pardew the US envoy at the time and if you look further up in the document it refers to the event of Ljuboten. And this is what Ambassador Pardew said in reaction to those events: "Speaking in Sofia, Bulgaria, earlier Friday, US envoy James Pardew said that despite the violence he was optimistic a peace deal would be signed on Monday as agreed to Wednesday by Macedonian rival parties." And then there's a quote. He says this: "No one supports the Albanian extremists, certainly not the United States nor any of our European allies. Said Pardew who helped oversee the peace talks." Then he said: "The use the force by Albanian extremists in Macedonia is unacceptable and totally rejected by the United States." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if perhaps you could scroll back up to the top of the document, you will see on the third paragraph the article referred to, inter alia, "the explosion that occurred some 10.6 miles north of the capital near the village of Ljubanci and Ljuboten when a convoy of army trucks drove over a land-mine." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that your mine attacks, in particular those two mine attacks on the 8th and 10th of August of 2001, gave rise to condemnation by the president of the Security Council of the United Nations. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that condemnation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Exhibit 1D15. It has been used last week, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recall that you've indicated your belief that documents coming from the Macedonian authorities covering the period July to September were unreliable. I think you repeated that quite a number of times. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the dates are as of early February till the late September.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D166, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is one of the UBK documents which was shown to you by my colleague of the Prosecutor. I hope you will recall or remember this particular document. Can you remember it?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, please. Do you recall that you were being asked about a number of individuals who are listed as members of the NLA from the village of Ljuboten. Do you recall being read out those names and giving your opinion about those?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in response to a number of them, you said that you did not know them or him. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I knew Refedin from this list and Baki. I may as well know the others, but I have to see them first.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Refedin is Refedin Selimi. Is that correct, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was one Refedin from Ljuboten. I don't know if there were other Refedins from that village. But I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you said that you did not know whether some of the others, some of the other persons, that did you not know were or were not members of the NLA, you did not wish to suggest that they were not. Your evidence was simply that you don't know. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I maybe know them, but only if I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You recall, Mr. Bushi, that you've told the Prosecution and repeated before this Chamber that in June of 2001 when you were arrested, you said you saw patches on the arms of a number of men with the Lions on it. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting it to you, Mr. Bushi, that again this is not true. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that when you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in June of 2004, you never mentioned any members of the Lions unit being present during that incident. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, but I don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you didn't mention any member of any special units either. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned that there was a number of policemen and special units. Now I don't remember what I said exactly, but it is true that they arrested me, and I told them that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what you said is this. It's at paragraph 2 of your statement: "On 9th of June 2001, I was arrested. About 100 uniformed policemen, military and men in plain clothes came to my house and made a search." Do you agree that there was no reference to any members of the Lions or any special units, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I did not mention that name at the time, but it was Lions who came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did not mention this name either, two years later when the Prosecution came back to have your statement read and signed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be. But now I'm telling you that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if half a dozen witnesses were to appear in this court to testify that, at that time, the Lions unit had not yet been set up, and if documents would support this evidence, they would all be wrong. Is that correct, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen them with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've also claimed to have seen them during riots in Skopje. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's information which you said you obtained from the media. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did not seek to verify that information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I verified it by the information I had and through some persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what was that information you had and the persons you contacted, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information that members of the Lions unit were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And from whom did you receive that information, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see. And you also remember telling the Prosecutor that during those riots, Mr. Boskoski's car was burned by the mob. Do you recall telling them that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for your patience Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I was ahead of myself, Your Honour. I'm unfortunately reminded that there's a number of documents which I would seek to tender at this stage. Perhaps that may occupy the last minutes of the day. Your Honour, the first document which the Defence would seek to tender is a collection of documents obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor from the German authorities. It's -- it appears on the Prosecution exhibit list as Rule 65 ter 284 and it has been identified as 1D829 by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour. We had in our 65 ter list a full version of this document. Which is not exactly the 65 ter document that my learned colleague seeks to tender, which is actually 45 pages. We are aware that this document has been put to the witness at least -- on a couple of occasions, but based on a ruling last week that some documents were admitted for the purpose of testing the credibility of this witness not necessarily for the truth of its content. The Prosecution is wondering whether my learned colleague is seeking to tender the document with the same intention because if this is the case, we are talking about a document of 45 pages and the witness has only been shown a small extracts of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think it has a double purpose. It's -- some of the information that is contained in this document as indicated by my colleague has been put by myself, but I believe also by the Prosecutor herself. The document is relevant not only some of the fact to which it testifies, but also as correctly pointed out by colleague to the credibility of this witness who has been denying a number of incidents or a number of facts which are recorded in this document. So it is relevant both, Your Honour, to some of the factual matter reported in the document and to the credibility of this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, have I understood you correctly. There is a document of some 45 pages which has been obtained from a European government and it deals, from what we have seen of it, with aspects of the affairs in Macedonia at the relevant time. Now you've put to the witness one or two aspects. But you now want to tender the 45 pages. On what basis is it going to be relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, there are two things, Your Honour, we believe that the Chamber could take into consideration. We believe that some other parts of document may be used at a later stage. So that's more the practical consideration having the entire document which would avoid having a piecemeal approach. Second one is, we believed it concerns the entire relevant period of approximately ten days or 15 days during this period and there are other aspects of this document which may be relevant to your consideration. If, however, the Chamber were aware of the view that at this stage only those parts which have been put to the witness should be tendered, we could either do that, Your Honour. Or perhaps if is it more agreeable to you we could mark the entire document as an MFI and if and when the document is further used with another witness, we could then seek to tender the entire document, not to divide it into pieces. Or if it is not being used by either the Prosecution or ourselves it would then seek to tender only those specific aspect of the document which have been used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The last course appears to the Chamber to be the appropriate one. It should be marked for identification as a document at the moment. And it will be left to counsel, whether at some later stage if the document is used or not used to seek to tender as an exhibit any part of it that is seen to justify admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit 1D229, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The second document, Your Honour, which the Defence would seek to tender at this stage was identified as Rule 65 ter 54. That's again from the Prosecution Rule 65 ter list and this is the record of meeting of the Security Council on the 7th of March, 2001 which has been considered quite extensively with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D230, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is a record, a transcript of a press briefing of the United States State Department which again has been put extensively to Mr. Bushi. It is dated the 30th of April of 2001, and it is Rule 65 ter 1D818.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You put into the record those parts of that briefing that were relevant. You read them to the witness. Why is the document itself going to be of any relevance so as to justify its admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The only reason, Your Honour, really is one of caution in case the transcript does not reflect the exact contents of the document, whether it is by fault of the pronunciation of the counsel or by any other reason. It is more a security that Your Honour can rely on the exact wording of the document. Other than that, Your Honour is quite correct that there would be no other valid purposes at this stage, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D231, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 1D712. This is a report or a collection of information by the Balkan Human Rights organisation which is associated with the Helsinki Committee which was put in several of its parts to the witness. It is Rule 65 ter 1D712.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Our quick scanning of the transcript of Friday suggests out of caution we should receive this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D232, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next document, Your Honour, is an UNMIK news. It is the United Nations interim administration mission in Kosovo. And again, I believe on Friday a passage of that document was put to the witness. It was Rule 65 ter 1D852. And we seek to tender it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For the same reason it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D233, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we also ask that a Rule 65 ter 1D233 be marked for identification. Only one passage was put to the witness, it will be used again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D234, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is Rule 65 ter 1D286. It is a joint statement by President Bush and Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder dated the 29th of March, 2001, and it was again put to the witness in the course of Friday, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're getting well down what we feel is a wrong road of admission, Mr. Mettraux, but out of caution because of some problems with the transcript, we will receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is Rule 65 ter 1D117. This is the presidential order by President George Bush dated the 26th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D236, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Next document, is the accompanying statement by the press secretary of the White House. It is Rule 65 ter 1D715.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are there more, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There are four more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're already over time. I think we must adjourn, and we will deal with the balance of them when we resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
